objective: Construct a fresh historical CS cohort whose frozen questions have objectively checkable formal, program-property, security-policy, or benchmark endpoints, then test whether direct outcome observability improves over the prior retrieval-focused cohort.

selection_provenance.source_frame_scope: arXiv-derived year/topic frame with year-end-safe metadata; latest metadata records revised after the year end were excluded from the frame.
selection_provenance.selection_rule: The fixed source frame was sampled before source-section eligibility screening. No later citation, outcome, benchmark result, or present-day popularity feature was used for selection; ineligible source-screen rows were retained in the denominator of the source-screen audit.
selection_provenance.followup_cutoff_rule: For each row, only primary evidence first public strictly after the row cutoff and no later than the fixed five-year followup end was admissible. Search was bounded; non-detection is missingness, never a negative label.

freeze_order: retain only a source-grounded open direction with a fixed object/property, comparator or baseline, measurable endpoint, and falsification gate
verify dated primary full text and classify dimensions independently
frozen_protocol.source_definition: An eligible question must be explicitly grounded in the inspected cutoff-version primary paper's open problem, formal property, complexity branch, security policy/property, program property, or public benchmark target. Reviewer-created generalizations are ineligible.
frozen_protocol.direct_outcome_rule: Direct support or refutation requires a dated primary source matching the frozen object, intervention or comparator, endpoint, and success/falsification condition. A different task, proxy metric, implementation-only follow-up, same-team case study, or adjacent benchmark is not direct resolution.
frozen_protocol.falsification_rule: Each row's claim fails when the prespecified endpoint shows no benefit/non-inferiority or violates its fixed safety, correctness, generalization, or complexity condition. Absence of an admissible result is not falsification.
frozen_protocol.paper3_gate: Do not fit or score Paper 3 because the direct outcome class has zero positive and zero negative labels and all six direct outcomes remain unadjudicated.

rows.title: Explainable Software Bot Contributions: Case Study of Automated Bug Fixes

source.source_basis: The source explicitly proposes an explainable repair package containing a patch, explanation, and behavioral-difference example, and identifies explanation clarity/patch essence as an open evaluation direction.

rows.frozen_question: For automated repair proposals from the same repair bot, does attaching a natural-language explanation plus a concrete behavioral-difference example improve blinded reviewer acceptance or time-to-decision compared with a patch-only proposal, at matched patch correctness and review workload?
rows.objective_endpoint: Blinded reviewer acceptance, understanding, and time-to-decision on identical patch units with patch correctness held constant.
rows.falsification_gate: No prespecified improvement, or a penalty after controlling for patch correctness, fails the proposed communication benefit; explanation preference without an acceptance, understanding, or time endpoint is insufficient.
rows.followup_observed: A 2023 primary study rated LLM-generated explanations for 30 Defects4J patches, reporting explanation correctness/completeness, but had no patch-only control and no reviewer acceptance or decision-time endpoint.

followup_sources.title: Evaluating Explanations for Software Patches Generated by Large Language Models

rows.uncertainty: The follow-up assessed explanation content on a small patch set, not the frozen causal presentation comparison.
rows.next_falsifiable_action: Run a preregistered patch-only versus explainable-package reviewer experiment with identical patches, blinded randomization, acceptance/understanding/time endpoints, and independent reviewers.

rows.title: Repairing Deep Neural Networks: Fix Patterns and Challenges

source.source_basis: The source identifies DNN-aware repair/localization, dimension-mismatch regressions, and vulnerability-introducing fixes as unresolved directions.

rows.frozen_question: On held-out DNN bug-fix instances, does a DNN-aware repair/localization intervention reduce incorrect or vulnerability-introducing patches relative to a code-only repair baseline while preserving verified bug-fix success?
rows.objective_endpoint: Project-disjoint verified fix success, regression rate, and security-relevant regression rate.
rows.falsification_gate: No reduction in independently verified regressions at non-inferior fix success, or a reduction that disappears under project-disjoint evaluation, fails the DNN-aware value claim.
rows.followup_observed: DeepDiagnosis studied diagnosis and recommendations without automated fixes; a 2023 DNN architecture-repair benchmark compared repair methods on performance repair and found random baselines competitive in some settings. Neither tested the frozen DNN-aware versus code-only regression/security comparison.

followup_sources.title: DeepDiagnosis: Automatically Diagnosing Faults and Recommending Actionable Fixes in Deep Learning Programs
Repairing DNN Architecture: Are We There Yet?

rows.uncertainty: The follow-ups use different intervention boundaries and endpoints; their method comparisons cannot be interpreted as causal evidence about vulnerability-introducing patches.
rows.next_falsifiable_action: Evaluate project-disjoint DNN repair units with code-only and DNN-aware arms, verified fix/regression/security checks, and independent model/data units.

rows.title: Security and Privacy Analyses of Internet of Things Children's Toys

source.cutoff_version: v2, public before the 2018 year-end cutoff
source.source_basis: The source analyzes three connected toys and explicitly motivates auditing more toys and mapping vague privacy policies to verifiable technical properties.

rows.frozen_question: Across a preregistered sample of connected children's toys, can an automated policy-to-property audit recover the same objectively verifiable privacy and network-security violations as independent manual analysis while reducing analyst effort without increasing false negatives?
rows.objective_endpoint: Violation recall, false-positive rate, and analyst time against an independently blinded manual audit on the same firmware/network traces.
rows.falsification_gate: The automation fails if recall is materially lower, false positives exceed the predeclared margin, or analyst-time savings disappear after ambiguous policy language is reviewed.
rows.followup_observed: The bounded search found no primary follow-up matching the automated policy-to-property versus manual audit with the frozen recall, false-positive, and effort endpoints.
rows.uncertainty: Later toy-risk syntheses and regulatory guidance were not primary controlled tests of the frozen audit comparison; search non-detection is not evidence of openness or failure.
rows.next_falsifiable_action: Freeze a larger toy sample, policy-to-property ontology, blinded manual adjudication, and recall/false-positive/effort margins before running the audit.

rows.title: SERENIoT: Collaborative Network Security Policy Management and Enforcement for Smart Homes

source.source_basis: The source explicitly leaves collaborative whitelist convergence under richer behavior and adversarial observations open, with observable policy and security/performance tradeoffs.

rows.frozen_question: For heterogeneous smart-home devices with software-update and adversarial-traffic regimes, can collaborative whitelist learning converge to a stable permitted-connection set while keeping false blocking and attacker-injected allowance below predeclared thresholds?
rows.objective_endpoint: Convergence time, false-block rate, attacker-allowance rate, and policy size against a fixed manufacturer/local-observation baseline.
rows.falsification_gate: Failure to converge within the fixed horizon, or either false blocking or attacker allowance exceeding the fixed safety margin relative to baseline, falsifies the claim.
rows.followup_observed: A 2022 public dissertation explicitly narrowed the unresolved issue to cross-device traffic/policy generalization and field robustness, but did not provide a matched collaborative-whitelist test with the frozen metrics.

followup_sources.title: Making Interactions With Home IoT Devices More Secure, Private, and Usable
followup_sources.locator: discussion of allowlist generalization and SERENIoT

rows.uncertainty: The dissertation date is a public mailing-list date bound rather than an independently authenticated deposit date, and it cannot supply a direct efficacy label.
rows.next_falsifiable_action: Run device-disjoint benign/update/adversarial traces with frozen convergence and safety thresholds, comparing collaborative and local/manufacturer policies.

rows.title: Towards an Automated Unified Framework to Run Applications for Combinatorial Interaction Testing

source.locator: PDF pp. 1-3; p. 10 conclusion and solver plan
source.source_basis: The source explicitly plans constraint handling through a solver and evaluates a public combinatorial interaction-testing framework on configuration spaces.

rows.frozen_question: On constrained virtual-machine configuration spaces, does adding solver-backed constraint handling to Avocado reduce invalid or redundant test executions while preserving or improving detection of invalid configurations relative to unconstrained t-way generation?
rows.objective_endpoint: Invalid-configuration detection recall, executed-test count, invalid-test rate, and wall-clock cost on the same configuration models.
rows.falsification_gate: No reduction in invalid/redundant executions at non-inferior detection recall, or a benefit that disappears on held-out configuration models, falsifies practical value.
rows.followup_observed: A 2020 Avocado follow-up reports solver-backed constrained interaction testing and an industrial-scale application, but the bounded primary record does not authenticate a matched unconstrained baseline with the frozen detection and cost endpoints.

followup_sources.title: Avocado: Open-Source Flexible Constrained Interaction Testing for Practical Application

rows.uncertainty: The follow-up is same-project lineage and implementation/case-study evidence; exact configuration models and matched baseline denominators were not authenticated for the direct endpoint.
rows.next_falsifiable_action: Pin both Avocado versions and run a held-out configuration-model comparison of solver-constrained and unconstrained generation with exact recall, invalid-test, count, and cost denominators.

rows.title: An Advanced Approach for Choosing Security Patterns and Checking their Implementation

source.source_basis: The source checks LTL behavioral properties for Web applications and explicitly identifies applications/patterns lacking UML sequence diagrams as an unresolved generalization boundary.

rows.frozen_question: Can the security-pattern checking approach generalize from UML-sequence-diagram-supported Web applications to applications or patterns lacking those diagrams by using code annotations, while preserving independently verified behavioral-property detection precision and recall?
rows.objective_endpoint: Project-disjoint behavioral-property detection precision and recall, annotation effort, and runtime.
rows.falsification_gate: Generalization fails if precision or recall falls beyond the predeclared margin, annotations cannot be independently checked, or the result depends on the design projects.
rows.followup_observed: The bounded search found adjacent security-pattern detection and conceptual pattern work, but no primary result matching the proposed annotation representation against the UML-sequence-diagram pipeline on independently checked properties.
rows.uncertainty: Adjacent detection frameworks differ in input representation, intervention, and endpoints; they are not direct evidence for or against the frozen question.
rows.next_falsifiable_action: Implement and preregister an annotation-versus-UML representation comparison on project-disjoint applications/patterns with independent property labels and fixed precision/recall margins.

observed_result.direct_label_missingness: 6/6 direct outcomes unadjudicated; no search failure was converted into a negative label

comparison_with_prior_retrieval_focused_.interpretation: Doubling the eligible-question count and using more explicitly objective source endpoints did not produce an observed direct positive or negative label. The fresh cohort improves endpoint specification and records structured partial/scope trajectories, but not direct outcome observability.

uncertainty: The six-row cohort is a deterministic hash-priority sample from a lexically filtered arXiv-derived frame, not a representative CS population.
Source screening reviewed targeted sections of exact cutoff-version primary full texts; it is not exhaustive page-by-page annotation.
Follow-up retrieval was bounded and cannot distinguish true absence from inaccessible or undiscovered evidence.
Partial progress and scope narrowing are not direct resolution, refutation, or Paper 3 labels.
The descriptive binomial interval is not a population prevalence estimate and no Paper 3 scoring, calibration, or forecast accuracy is claimed.
next_falsifiable_action: Run one or more preregistered, endpoint-matched follow-ups beginning with solver-constrained Avocado testing or SERENIoT cross-device policy evaluation; retain direct missingness unless a dated primary result matches the frozen object, comparator, metric, and falsification gate.
